name: Cloistered Scholar Scholar Archetype
body:
Cloistered scholars tend to be more secluded than others of their ilk, sequestering themselves away in a library, university, or monastery, and dedicating their lives to lives of pure research and academia.

Cloistered Studies

You cannot choose from the studies of Alchemy, Arcana, or Economics. Instead, you gain access to the Chirography and Theology studies (see below), which are only available to cloistered scholars.

This feature modifies scholar studies.

Librarian

At 1st level, choose a favored enemy, as the ranger class feature. At 4th level and every 4 levels thereafter, you gain another favored enemy. At 8th and 16th levels, you can raise your bonus against one favored enemy (including the favored enemy you just selected) by 2, but otherwise your bonus against each enemy does not change and remains at +2. You must keep detailed notes about each favored enemy in a separate journal, each of which weighs a minimum of 1 pound. You must keep each favored enemy journal on your person at all times—in hand, stored in a backpack, or the like—in order to gain any bonus from this ability against that favored enemy. If you ever lose one of your journals, you can replace it by buying a blank journal (10 gp) and spending one hour working to recommit your notes to writing.

This feature replaces techniques.

Chirography

Associated Skill Profession (scribe) (Wis)

Basic Study Ability
Scrivener (Ex)

At 1st level, you gain Scribe Scroll as a bonus feat. With one hour of work every morning, you can hastily prepare one scroll of any spell or spell-like ability that you know or can prepare from the scholar class. Alternately, you can prepare a scroll of any one of the following spells: alarm, comprehend languages, detect magic, erase, floating disk, identify, or unseen servant. This uses no inspiration points, even if it normally requires you to use them, and incurs no cost unless the spell has an expensive material component.

You never need to make a Use Magic Device check to activate one of these hastily prepared scrolls. However, anyone else treats these scrolls as if the spell were not on their spell list, even if it normally would be. A scroll made using this ability can only be read for 24 hours, after which it loses its potency and the words fade from the page.

You can never have more than one hastily prepared scroll from this ability at a time.

The work of hastily preparing a scroll can be done during the hour that you review your notebooks and prepare your other abilities for the day. If you don’t otherwise have a caster level, use your ranks in Profession (scribe) as your caster level and Intelligence as your spellcasting statistic.

Associated Technique n/a (There is no technique associated with the Chirography study.)

Advanced Study Abilities
Calligraphy (Ex)

Prerequisite(s): Scrivener study ability, scholar level 4th.

You can use your ranks in Profession (scribe) to write in calligraphy, creating works of art.

In addition, you gain any one 1st- or 2nd-level bardic masterpiece, which you write in calligraphy in scroll-like form. You must meet any listed prerequisites for your masterpiece, using your ranks in Profession (scribe) in place of any Perform skill listed.

To use your masterpiece, you must draw this scroll as a move action and read it aloud rather than using the Perform skill indicated.

When you reach 7th ranks in Profession (scribe), you may craft one additional calligraphy masterpiece of no higher than 3rd level. When you reach 10th ranks in Profession (scribe), you may craft one additional calligraphy masterpiece of no higher than 4th level. While using your masterpieces, you may use a maximum number of rounds of bardic performance each day equal to your number of ranks in Profession (scribe).

Illumination (Ex)

Prerequisite(s): Scrivener study ability, scholar level 2nd.

You can use light at will as a spell-like ability.

By expending 1 point of inspiration, you can use sun metal as a spell-like ability. When you reach 4 ranks in profession (scribe), you can expend 2 points of inspiration to use faerie fire as a spell-like ability. When you reach 7 ranks in profession (scribe), you can expend 3 points of inspiration to use daylight as a spell-like ability. You must hold a writing instrument in hand as a focus when using any of these spell-like abilities. (Drawing this focus is a free action if you have a hand free.) If you do not use such a focus, you must succeed at a concentration check (DC 15 + the ability’s inspiration cost) or you fail to cast the spell—although in such a case you do not expend any inspiration points.

Runecasting (Ex)

Prerequisite(s): Profession (scribe) 3 ranks, Scrivener study ability, scholar level 3rd.

Each day, you can prepare one elementally-charged rune for every 3 ranks you possess in Profession (scribe). You can place these runes on a creature, an item, or a runestone.

Each rune take one minute to paint, carve, or otherwise create. Some effects require multiple runes, and require one minute per rune to inscribe.

Regardless of the number of runes used to create an effect, activating it requires a standard action. The runestone or the general area containing the rune must be touched while the rune’s name is spoken aloud. If the rune was placed on a runestone, that runestone must be held at the location where the spell is to originate or be centered, and the runestone is then consumed in the process of activating the spell. If placed on a person or object, that person or object must be the target of the spell; the rune glows faintly while the spell is active and then disappears.

Neither scribing nor activating runes expends points from your inspiration pool.

Anyone can activate a rune once it is placed on an object or runestone, but a rune placed on a person can only be activated by that person. A rune can only be activated during the day in which it was scribed. If it is not activated before you complete your next long rest, it loses its potency and fades away.

The caster level for all rune effects is equal to your number of ranks in Profession (scribe), and the DC is 10 + your Intelligence modifier + the number of runes used to create the effect. You can increase the DC of an effect by using extra runes to create the effect, if you have additional runes to spare, but you cannot otherwise modify a rune effect through metamagic or other means.

At 3 ranks in profession (scribe), you can create effects that require 1 rune. At 6 ranks in profession (scribe), you can create effects that require 2 runes. Finally, at 9 ranks in profession (scribe), you can create effects that require 3 runes.

Symbology (Ex)

Prerequisite(s): Profession (scribe) 3 ranks, Scrivener study ability, scholar level 3rd.

Your practiced study of written characters, glyphs, signs, and symbols has provided you with a preternatural insight into the underlying patterns of the behavior of the creatures that use them. Once per day, you can interpret the signs to influence the behavior of those around you and change the course of fate.

At the beginning of each day, draw one card from an ordinary deck of cards. This card determines what kind of result you can affect. At any point during that day, you can force your target to re-roll one d20 roll of the appropriate type, as determined by your card. The target must take the result of the second roll. To be an eligible target, a creature must have an Intelligence score of at least 3, must be within 100 feet of you, and you must have line of effect to the target. Using this ability does not require an action.

Targets by Suit: ? yourself only, ? any ally, ? any hostile creature, ? anyone.

J Reflex saving throw, ?? Q Will saving throw, ?? K Fortitude saving throw, ?? A any d20 roll, ?? joker (optional rule; any target) any d% roll.

When you reach 6 ranks in Profession (scribe), you can draw 2 cards and keep the one you want to use that day. When you reach 9 ranks in Profession (scribe), you can draw 3 cards and keep the one you want to use. When you reach 12 ranks in Profession (scribe), you can draw 4 cards and keep any 2 to use during that day; you can only use one card on a given roll. When you reach 15 ranks in Profession (scribe), you can draw 5 cards and keep 2 to use. Finally, when you reach 18 ranks in Profession (scribe), you can draw 6 cards and keep any 3 to use throughout the day.
